subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: Should OpenClaw silently drop unconfigured-provider/Codex failures at the provider/routing boundary, or normalize them into safe generic user-facing copy while keeping diagnostics internal?
rationale: The parser gap is a bounded bug, but the requested silent discard changes user-visible failure semantics and observability for provider routing, subagents, and channel delivery.

options.title: Parser plus explicit routing policy
options.body: Add `detail` parser/sanitizer coverage now and define when unconfigured-provider failures become no-reply versus generic safe copy, with tests across assistant error and sanitizer delivery paths.

options.title: Formatter-only repair
options.body: Treat this issue as a safe-copy bug by parsing `detail` payloads, while tracking silent unconfigured-provider suppression separately.

options.title: Keep current generic fallback
options.body: Accept the current assistant-error generic fallback as enough and require a fresh live Telegram repro before changing parser or routing behavior.

recommendation.title: Parser plus explicit routing policy
recommendation.body: Add `detail` parser/sanitizer coverage now and define when unconfigured-provider failures become no-reply versus generic safe copy, with tests across assistant error and sanitizer delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent adjacent history on user-facing provider-error suppression and the remaining blocker is the product policy for channel-visible failures.
